# Agent 2: API + Data

## Your Role
Build the complete backend — API routes, retailer adapters, cron pipeline, and seed data. The database schema is already deployed to Neon PostgreSQL via Prisma v7.

## Before You Start
You are building a production app for real users — not a demo, not a prototype. Every route you create should be production-ready.

Read every file in `.gemini/antigravity/brain/` — especially api-contract.md.
Read `.antigravity/rules.md` for code quality and security rules.

## Important Context
- Database is ALREADY set up — Prisma schema is deployed to Neon PostgreSQL
- `src/lib/db.ts` ALREADY exists with the Prisma v7 driver adapter (PrismaPg + pg.Pool)
- `src/generated/prisma/` has the generated client — DO NOT re-run prisma generate
- Models: Laptop, Price, PriceHistory, SearchSuggestion (with enums Category, DealRating)
- Auth: NONE for v1 (no user accounts)
- 16 retailer sources: 4 API-based + 12 scraped (see api-contract.md for full list)
- Cron endpoints protected by CRON_SECRET header

## Files You OWN (create and edit freely)
- `src/app/api/**/*` (all API routes)
- `src/lib/retailers/*` (retailer adapter implementations)
- `src/lib/validators/*` (Zod schemas for request validation)
- `src/lib/deal-rating.ts` (deal rating computation logic)
- `src/lib/spec-normalizer.ts` (Gemini API integration for spec normalization)
- `prisma/seed.ts` (seed data script)
- `src/__tests__/api/*` (API tests)

## Files You Must NOT Touch
- `prisma/schema.prisma` (already deployed — do not modify)
- `src/lib/db.ts` (already configured — use as-is)
- `src/generated/prisma/*` (already generated — use as-is)
- `src/components/*` (Foundation and Feature agents own these)
- `src/app/(features)/*` (Feature agents own these)
- `src/app/page.tsx` (Foundation agent owns this)
- `.gemini/antigravity/brain/*` (Cowork manages these)

## Build Order

1. **Create `src/lib/validators/laptop.ts`** — Zod schemas for laptop query params (category, brand, minPrice, maxPrice, minRam, gpuBrand, cpuBrand, sortBy, order, page, limit, q). Export as `laptopQuerySchema`.

2. **Create `src/lib/api-error.ts`** — Error handler wrapper. Standard error format from api-contract.md: `{ error: { code, message, details } }`. Error codes: VALIDATION_ERROR, NOT_FOUND, RATE_LIMITED, INTERNAL_ERROR. Export `withErrorHandler` HOF and `ApiError` class.

3. **Create `src/lib/validate.ts`** — Request validation utility. `validateQuery(request, schema)` parses URL search params against a Zod schema. Returns typed result or throws ApiError.

4. **Build `src/app/api/laptops/route.ts`** — GET handler. Accepts all query params from api-contract.md. Uses Prisma to query with dynamic where/orderBy. Returns top 3 prices per laptop (not all). Includes pagination. Cache-Control: `public, s-maxage=60, stale-while-revalidate=120`.

5. **Build `src/app/api/laptops/[slug]/route.ts`** — GET handler. Returns full laptop detail with ALL retailer prices (not just top 3). Includes ramType, storageInterface, reviewSummary, releaseDate. Cache-Control: `public, s-maxage=30, stale-while-revalidate=60`.

6. **Build `src/app/api/deals/route.ts`** — GET handler. Laptops sorted by discount percentage descending. Optional category filter and limit.

7. **Build `src/app/api/budget-picks/route.ts`** — GET handler. Algorithm: weight RAM, storage, CPU benchmark proxy against price. Optional category and maxPrice filters.

8. **Build `src/app/api/best-rated/route.ts`** — GET handler. Laptops sorted by reviewScore descending. minReviewScore param (default 70).

9. **Build `src/app/api/filters/route.ts`** — GET handler. Returns dynamic filter values with counts. Only values that have matching laptops. Cache-Control: `public, s-maxage=300`.

10. **Build `src/app/api/search/suggestions/route.ts`** — GET handler. Typeahead search. Minimum 2 chars. Returns suggestions grouped by type (laptop, brand, spec). Limit default 8.

11. **Create retailer adapter interface** — `src/lib/retailers/types.ts` with `RetailerAdapter` and `RawProduct` interfaces per api-contract.md.

12. **Build retailer adapters** — One file per tier:
    - `src/lib/retailers/amazon.ts` — PA-API integration
    - `src/lib/retailers/bestbuy.ts` — Best Buy API
    - `src/lib/retailers/walmart.ts` — Walmart Affiliate API
    - `src/lib/retailers/ebay.ts` — eBay Browse API
    - `src/lib/retailers/scraper-major.ts` — Newegg, B&H, Micro Center, Adorama
    - `src/lib/retailers/scraper-manufacturer.ts` — Lenovo, Dell, HP, Apple
    - `src/lib/retailers/scraper-warehouse.ts` — Costco, Sam's Club, Target, Office Depot/Staples
    - `src/lib/retailers/index.ts` — Registry that exports all adapters

13. **Create `src/lib/spec-normalizer.ts`** — Gemini API integration. Takes raw scraped spec strings, returns structured fields (cpuBrand, cpuModel, gpuBrand, gpuModel, ramType, storageInterface, displayType, etc.).

14. **Build `src/app/api/cron/refresh-prices/route.ts`** — POST handler. Protected by `Authorization: Bearer ${CRON_SECRET}`. Iterates all retailer adapters, fetches products, normalizes specs via Gemini, upserts Laptop + Price records, records PriceHistory. Returns per-retailer success/error counts.

15. **Build `src/app/api/cron/compute-deals/route.ts`** — POST handler. Protected by CRON_SECRET. For each laptop: find lowest price across retailers, compute median, assign dealRating (GREAT if ≥15% below, FAIR if within 15%, ABOVE_AVERAGE if >15% above). Update denormalized fields: lowestPrice, lowestRetailer, dealRating.

16. **Create `src/lib/deal-rating.ts`** — Export `computeDealRating(prices: number[]): { rating: DealRating, lowestPrice: number, lowestRetailer: string, median: number }`.

17. **Create `prisma/seed.ts`** — Realistic seed data: ~50 laptops across Work/Gaming/Apple categories with prices from 3-5 retailers each. Use real laptop names and realistic specs. This makes the app look populated during development.

18. **Write API tests** — At least one success + one error test per route. Test query param validation, 404 for missing slugs, cron auth check.

19. Run `npm test` to verify all API tests pass.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every endpoint in api-contract.md has a working route
- [ ] Every route uses withErrorHandler and returns standard error format
- [ ] Every route returns the exact response shape from api-contract.md
- [ ] Query param validation via Zod on all list endpoints
- [ ] Cache-Control headers set correctly per endpoint
- [ ] Cron endpoints reject requests without valid CRON_SECRET
- [ ] All 16 retailer adapters implement the RetailerAdapter interface
- [ ] Gemini spec normalizer works for scraped product data
- [ ] Deal rating computation is correct (GREAT/FAIR/ABOVE_AVERAGE thresholds)
- [ ] Seed data populates ~50 realistic laptops
- [ ] All API tests pass
- [ ] No raw SQL — all queries through Prisma

## Coordination
You run in parallel with the Foundation and Feature agents — no dependencies between you.
The Feature agents will call your API routes using the paths from api-contract.md.
To avoid integration issues:
- Follow api-contract.md EXACTLY for route paths, methods, and response shapes
- Export Zod schemas from `src/lib/validators/` so Feature agents can import for client-side validation
- Use the exact endpoint paths — don't rename routes
- The `db` import comes from `@/lib/db` — already configured
